movesets.name: Substitute + Swords Dance
movesets.description: These sample sets were uploaded on January 27, 2024 and are up-to-date for the current BW LC metagame.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Inner Focus lets Pawniard ignore flinches from Persian's Fake Out, but Persian is unlikely to revenge kill Pawniard with a weak and resisted move, and the protection Defiant gives from Intimidate is more useful for a physical attacker like Pawniard. Brick Break is stronger than Low Kick against Clefairy and opposing Pawniard and still 2HKOes Lairon, but it's weaker against heavy foes like Walrein, Slaking, and Munchlax. Pawniard has utility options in its movepool like Thunder Wave, Taunt, and Knock Off, but Clefairy, Solrock, and Wormadam-S are all better utility Pokemon than Pawniard thanks to their better bulk. Magnet Rise protects Pawniard from Ground-type moves from Wormadam-S, Vibrava, and Hippopotas to turn them into setup fodder, but Pawniard has to give up a vital coverage option and worsen its matchups against its checks.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Pawniard is OHKOed by almost any Fighting-type move. Mienfoo is very common and requires significant chip damage before Pawniard can threaten to KO it, even with a boost from Swords Dance. Mienfoo is hard to wear down if it has Regenerator and Eviolite, but its frailty, Reckless, or a Choice Scarf can open windows for Pawniard overwhelm it. Muk, Kingler, and Shelgon commonly run Fighting-type moves for coverage. Although Pignite is rare, it's very bulky and resists Pawniard's STAB combination.

Steel-types: Steel-types take little damage from Pawniard's STAB moves, though Lairon is 2HKOed by Low Kick and Wormadam-S without Hidden Power Ground struggles against Swords Dance Pawniard. Magnemite is rare, but it can trap and remove Pawniard.

Water-types: Whiscash and Pelipper are bulky, resist Iron Head, and pressure Pawniard because of its frailty. Frillish and Staryu can manuever around Sucker Punch with Recover and threaten Pawniard with burns from Will-O-Wisp and Scald. Pawniard isn't totally helpless against these foes, though, as Sucker Punch can let it beat offensive Water-types with good prediction, Staryu is relatively frail, and Frillish is Dark-weak and can be overwhelmed by Night Slash and prior Swords Dance boosts.

Ground-types and Ground-type Coverage: Vibrava and Hippopotas 2HKO Pawniard with their STAB moves, and both can stay healthy with their recovery moves, but Swords Dance boosts and Iron Head flinches can help Pawniard beat them. Meganium and Slaking possess good physical bulk and threaten Pawniard with Earthquake.

Substitute Attackers: With Substitute, even Dark-weak attackers like Grumpig can outplay Pawniard's Sucker Punch. Simisear and the uncommon Magmar roast Pawniard with their STAB moves; their greater Speed and STAB Fire-type moves bait Sucker Punch. Walrein and Kingler both outspeed Pawniard and overwhelm it due to its poor bulk.

Special Attackers: Even special attackers with STAB moves Pawniard resist like Glaceon and Choice Specs Meganium can beat Pawniard due to its lower special bulk. Raichu can overpower Pawniard, but its physical frailty leaves it vulnerable to Sucker Punch.

movesets.name: Wallbreaker
movesets.description:
When equipped with Swords Dance, Pawniard can leverage its solid STAB attacks, good coverage, and extremely powerful priority in Sucker Punch to cleave through defense and offense alike. Although Pawniard is still frail even when outfitted with Eviolite, its Dark / Steel typing has plenty of resistances, giving Pawniard setup opportunities against passive walls like Wormadam-S, Vullaby, and Clefairy lacking Thunder Wave. Pawniard can also set up on weaker physical attackers like Persian and Emolga and Choice-locked Pokemon like Mr. Mime, Grumpig, and Gastly. Pawniard's STAB Sucker Punch is a strong priority move that staves off frail would-be revenge killers like Simisear and Raichu, outright OHKOing them after a Swords Dance even though they are not weak to it. STAB Iron Head complements Sucker Punch, breaking physically defensive Pokemon like Solrock and Graveler, circumventing the chance to fail Sucker Punch has, and potentially flinching down walls like Clefairy, Hippopotas, and Vibrava. Pursuit provides Pawniard offensive utility, picking off weakened Dark-weak Pokemon, like Choice-locked Mr. Mime, Grumpig, and Gastly. Offensive pivots like Persian and Emolga often lack the coverage to significantly damage Pawniard and thus are also vulnerable to Pursuit. Night Slash is a strong, reliable Dark-type STAB move to beat Steel-resistant walls like Frillish, which resists Iron Head and can deny Sucker Punch by using Will-O-Wisp. Low Kick lets Pawniard break Lairon, which otherwise tanks Pawniard's STAB moves.

Pawniard fits on offensive teams, as they appreciate Pawniard's wallbreaking, potential to sweep, and decent defensive profile for a wallbreaker. Fast cleaners like Simisear, Raichu, and Mr. Mime greatly appreciate Pawniard breaking down defensive cores for them. Offensive pivots like Persian and Emolga help bring Pawniard in safely while luring in physical walls like Wormdam-S and Solrock for Pawniard to break. Mienfoo is a significant problem for Pawniard, so Muk and Arbok make helpful partners, while Pawniard can protect them from offensive Psychic-types like Grumpig and Mr. Mime. Setup sweepers like Shelgon and Leafeon benefit from Pawniard softening up physical walls so that they can sweep.

movesets.name: Offensive Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Pawniard's interesting typing makes it a unique choice for an offensive Stealth Rock setter, able to set up on opposing entry hazard setters like Solrock and non-Hidden Power Ground Wormadam-S. Sucker Punch finishes off frailer foes like Mr. Mime and Raichu; it also gives Pawniard more opportunities to set Stealth Rock. Iron Head is its most consistent STAB attack, notably hitting Solrock for a 2HKO while being faster than it, which prevents Solrock from aggressively switching into Pawniard like it could to Lairon. Its last slot is quite flexible: Pursuit traps and checkmates weakened foes like Emolga and Mr. Mime, Night Slash consistently threatens Frillish, Low Kick is its strongest option against Lairon and opposing Pawniard, and Swords Dance doubles up on its offensive capabilities by setting up on defensive threats like non-Hidden Power Ground Wormadam-T and Ivysaur.

Offensive partners like Persian and Mienfoo enjoy benefitting from Pawniard's utility and decent matchup against standard Solrock sets, though Pawniard must be wary of Will-O-Wisp. In addition, thanks to its access to Sucker Punch, Pawniard's teammates also appreciate it being a decent offensive check to Psychic-types like non-Substitute Grumpig and Mr. Mime, though it must be wary of Fighting-type coverage. In return, they can pivot Pawniard into the field more safely to circumvent its mediocre bulk. Setup sweepers like Grumpig and Simisear also benefit from Pawniard being a solid offensive switch-in to Persian, a revenge killer that would otherwise be a serious threat to offensive builds. In return, these setup sweepers can do well against some of Pawniard's weaknesses, like Grumpig and Simisear checking Mienfoo and Lairon, respectively.
